requirements.text: The RLCS Application will provide data to other external systems via an external server data store accessible by other external systems such as ATMS-2, ValuePricing/FasTrak, and ATIS.
The RLCS Application will also allow for remote access through a firewall via outside telecommunications networks by authorized users.
The RLCS software shall send to and receive data from the field device I/O cards through I/O driver software.
All external systems shall retrieve RLCS status from a server outside the RLCS network.

The system shall have a Graphical User Interface (GUI) that allows the operator to view system status, issue commands to change device status, configure the system, export log data, and generate reports.
The RLCS shall monitor all field device sensors, and shall process operator requests for changing field device status.
The RLCS shall execute stored operational control command sequences based on the current system mode of operation and the schedule for each sequence.
The RLCS must be available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year.
Remote access must be restricted to multi-factor authentication (MFA) over an encrypted VPN tunnel, with session timeouts and logging of all remote administrative actions.
Remote dial-in must utilize industry-standard encryption (e.g., AES-256) and secure authentication protocols, ensuring that the dial-up connection is not a clear-text vulnerability.
Message integrity must be verified using HMAC-SHA256 or digital signatures to prevent tampering with control commands.
Define 99.99% availability as 'excluding scheduled maintenance windows of X hours per month, measured as the percentage of time the system is capable of executing lane control commands from the TMC'.

Add a performance constraint: 'The system shall maintain all response time requirements (e.g., 2-second status updates) when the system is expanded to include the maximum defined configuration of 2 additional DCUs and 4 additional CMS units.'
Define the maximum allowable latency for external systems to receive status updates after a field device state change.
Define the maximum CPU/Memory overhead allowed for reporting tasks or require the use of a read-only replica database to ensure isolation.

OPEN: The PRD mentions password encryption but does not define the password policy (complexity, rotation, lockout). - The system shall enforce a password policy requiring a minimum of 12 characters, including complexity (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols), and enforce account lockout after 5 failed attempts.

OPEN: The PRD mentions an external server data store for external systems but does not define the security boundary or data sanitization requirements. - The external server must be physically or logically isolated (DMZ) from the primary RLCS control network, and data pushed to it must be sanitized to prevent injection attacks.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'degraded mode' and 'failure' but does not specify the maximum allowable latency for failover between redundant components or the expected state of field devices during a transition. - Specify the maximum failover time for the system to switch to a redundant controller or backup communication path without requiring manual intervention.

OPEN: The requirement for 2-second status updates conflicts with the potential network load and processing overhead of the reporting and database functions. - Explicitly state that monitoring and control traffic must be prioritized over reporting and database synchronization traffic to ensure the 2-second latency is met.

OPEN: The PRD specifies a 99.99% uptime requirement but does not define the expected concurrent user load or the maximum number of external system connections. - Specify the maximum number of concurrent GUI users and the maximum number of concurrent external system connections the server must support while maintaining the 99.99% availability target.

OPEN: The PRD mentions future expansion (two additional DCUs) but does not define the performance impact or the maximum allowable latency increase for the expanded network. - Define the performance degradation threshold (if any) allowed when the system is scaled to its maximum capacity.
